resources.string: This is where you keep everything you watch, read and listen to: films, series, anime, books and records, with your rating and your diary.
Searching films, series and anime needs your TMDB key (it’s free). You can also add them by hand.

Books: Open Library (Internet Archive), open data.
Music: MusicBrainz (public domain data) and covers from the Cover Art Archive.

Pick the file Netflix exports (your viewing activity CSV), Letterboxd (the ZIP or a CSV), Goodreads (the CSV) or Spotify (your history ZIP). From Netflix, Spotify and other apps you can also share something straight to El Cajón.
Save everything to a file whenever you like (keys aren’t included).
It’s merged with what you have; if something is in both, the newest wins.
To search films, series and anime, El Cajón uses TMDB, the largest open film database. TMDB asks each person to use their own key: it’s free and you only get it once.
1. Create a free account at themoviedb.org.\n2. In Settings → API, request a key (personal use).\n3. Copy the “API Key” (or the “API Read Access Token”) and paste it here.
The key stays encrypted on this phone and is only used to search. It isn’t in backups or sync.
El Cajón uses TMDB and the TMDB APIs but is not endorsed, certified, or otherwise approved by TMDB.
Connect your GitHub and your cajón saves itself to a private file in your account (a secret Gist). El Cajón on your PC reads that same file, so you have the same on both. It’s optional.
1. Tap Create token (GitHub opens with everything ready).\n2. Under Expiration choose No expiration or 1 year.\n3. Scroll down, tap Generate token, copy it and paste it here.
What’s on this phone stays. The file on your GitHub stays too (delete it there if you want).
The token stays encrypted on this phone. The file is secret: only someone with its link or your account can see it.
The token is invalid or expired.
The token has no gist permission.

resources.string: Film: TMDB (with your key). Music: MusicBrainz, covers from the Cover Art Archive and photos from Wikimedia Commons. Books: Open Library. Trending: Wikipedia and Wikidata, TMDB, ListenBrainz, Open Library and TVmaze.
Nothing here yet. Tap Search to add something.

Photos of artists, writers and directors from Wikimedia Commons, found through Wikidata (CC0 data) or as the free image of their Wikipedia article; for directors also TMDB’s, and for writers Open Library’s. Before using one, the app checks on the phone that it is a good size and shows a face; if none passes, there is no photo and the person can pick another or upload their own. Each Commons photo has its own free license and author, shown on the page. Short biographies are the introduction of the Wikipedia article (CC BY-SA 4.0), credited.

Spotify, YouTube Music or any app: what plays (at least 30 seconds) goes to “Recently heard”. It stays on this phone only.

Optional, if you have Premium: brings what you listen to, your saved albums and the artists you follow. Connects in 4 steps.
Spotify doesn’t let a free app connect on its own: each person creates their own “app” on Spotify (free, a couple of minutes) and El Cajón uses it only to read. You need Spotify Premium.
Sign in with your Spotify account. Give it any name and description, for example “My cajón”.
Open Spotify to create the app
In the same form, under “Redirect URIs” paste this address and tap Add. Further down tick “Web API”, accept the terms and save.
After saving, Spotify shows your app: copy the “Client ID” (32 letters and numbers), come back here and paste it.
That doesn’t look like a Client ID: it’s 32 letters (a to f) and numbers.
Spotify opens so you can accept. When done, come back to El Cajón.
If Spotify showed an error, it’s almost always the address from step 2 (it must be exact) or the Client ID. Cancel, check them and connect again.
It wasn’t accepted on Spotify. Connect again whenever you want.
Spotify didn’t come back. Check that the address from step 2 is saved exactly the same and connect again.
Spotify doesn’t recognize that Client ID. Copy it again from your app (step 3).
Spotify didn’t allow reading your account: it needs Premium and signing in with the same account you created the app with.
Couldn’t reach Spotify. Check your internet and try again.
The Client ID and the permission are stored encrypted only on this phone. El Cajón only reads: it never changes anything in your Spotify. You can disconnect it in Settings.
Further back? Ask Spotify for your “extended streaming history” (Account → Privacy) and pick the ZIP in “Bring from other apps”.
Turn on “Log what I listen to” in Settings and the albums playing in your apps show up here.
